data.name: PageTitle
data.value: Setup wizard: tuning the monitor with patterns

data.name: Intro
data.value: When the wizard starts, the blue light filter and extra dimming are turned off for a while and come back when it ends. Patterns never flash; you change the frames yourself. If you cancel, your monitor settings return to how they were before the wizard.

data.name: PatternKeys
data.value: Right arrow or Space: next frame · Left arrow: previous frame · Esc: close

data.name: SampleText
data.value: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. 0123456789

data.name: Step_WarmUpAndPosition_Text
data.value: Keep the monitor on for at least 30 minutes; the backlight drifts in the first minutes. Your eyes should be at or slightly below the top edge of the screen, at 70–80 cm. Room light should be your usual working light. In the OSD set Color: Custom RGB (for RGB gain), Sharpness: 4, Overscan: Off; in NVIDIA set output dynamic range: Full.

data.name: Step_BlackAndWhiteClipping_Text
data.value: First find the highest contrast on the light grey pattern (230–254): all neighboring steps should be distinguishable. Then set brightness on the dark grey pattern (1–25): the darkest steps should be visible but the black background should not glow. The backlight is used to raise brightness; contrast does not go above its starting value.

data.name: Step_Sharpness_Text
data.value: Choose the highest sharpness that adds no white line (halo) at text edges. Look at both dark text on a light background and light text on a dark background.

data.name: Step_FullRgbCheck_Text
data.value: The near-black steps 1–16 should stand out from the black background. If they do not, the output dynamic range in NVIDIA may be Limited: set it to Full.

data.name: Step_ViewingAngle_Text
data.value: The top, middle and bottom bands show the same grey. Adjust your chair or the monitor's tilt until they look equal: eyes at the top edge, tilt between 0° and −5°. Move your head up and down and watch how the difference changes.

data.name: Step_DeadPixelsAndUniformity_Text
data.value: Go through black, white, red, green and blue: a dot that never changes is a dead or stuck pixel. On the three grey frames look for bright or dark patches and light bleed in the corners.

data.name: Step_WhiteMatch_Text
data.value: Open a white page on the Pixel's screen in 'Natural' color mode and place it next to the monitor. Lower the red, green and blue gain until both whites look the same temperature (never raise: brightness drops). For RGB gain, Color: Custom RGB must be selected in the monitor's OSD.

data.name: Step_Gamma_Text
data.value: Open the gamma pattern and look from 2–3 meters away or with squinted eyes. Each frame has thin black-and-white lines on the left and flat grey on the right. Find the frame where the striped area and the flat grey look equally bright (the number under the grey identifies the frame) and select the same frame below. The choice is applied at once; if you open the pattern again, the 2.2 frame should now look equal.

data.name: Step_GreyBalance_Text
data.value: Open the grey balance pattern: dark, mid and light grey. Each grey should look colorless (neutral); you can compare with grey on the Pixel. If a grey looks tinted, lower that color slightly (pinkish: red or blue; greenish: green; bluish: blue). Go in small steps; it is applied when you release.

data.name: Idle
data.value: The wizard is off. When it starts, blue light, extra dimming and vibrance turn off for a while, and choosing profiles from the tray is disabled until the wizard ends.

data.name: WarmUpRemaining
data.value: Warm-up: about {0} min left. Waiting is optional, but measurements are more accurate after warm-up.

data.name: WarmUpDone
data.value: Warm-up time is over; you can start tuning.

data.name: MonitorSettings
data.value: Monitor settings (written once when you release the slider)

data.name: NoDdc
data.value: The monitor does not answer DDC: make this step's settings with the monitor's OSD buttons.

data.name: GpuWhite_Text
data.value: Without DDC, white matching is done with the graphics card's color table. You can only lower the channels (80–100%).

data.name: Gamma_Label
data.value: Panel gamma: the frame that looks most equal

data.name: Gamma_LastFrame
data.value: You closed the pattern on this frame: {0}. If that one looked equal, select it below.

data.name: Status_Started
data.value: The wizard started. Blue light, extra dimming and vibrance are temporarily off.

data.name: Status_Cancelled
data.value: Cancelled; settings changed by the wizard returned to their old values and effects are back.

data.name: Status_CancelPartial
data.value: Cancelled, but these did not return to their old values: {0}. Check them in the monitor's OSD.

data.name: Status_CalibrationRejected
data.value: Windows rejected this color table; the previous calibration stays. Try a smaller change.

data.name: Status_CalibrationOutOfRange
data.value: The choice is outside the allowed range; not applied.

data.name: Pattern_DeadPixels
data.value: Dead pixels (black, white, red, green, blue)
